_provenance.what: The paramparā as data (owner, 2026-10-08: "Do not make observation mandatory; India has observed for centuries — use those observations as data"). Every dated observation, determination, rule, doctrine and instrument operation of the Indian tradition that a local text or a local e-text states, each with its edition, page and line, its verbatim Sanskrit, its value in the text's own units, its assumptions and how the engine uses it. The owner's own attributions to texts that are not local are recorded as class owner-statement, status 'awaiting edition', and are upgraded to [text] when an edition is added.
_provenance.rules: Quotes are verbatim from the line named in 'from' (the e-text lines are copied, and only those lines, into etext-lines.json). No modern translation is copied: where an edition's own English or figure is the datum, it is marked as the editor's. Numbers are re-derived by parampara.test.js from the words (bhūtasaṅkhyā units first, or Kaṭapayādi through katapayadi.js) or from the printed figure the edition sets above the verse. The 15 eclipse records point into corpus/jyotirmimamsa/eclipses.json and readings.json, which stay their single source; nothing here repeats a reading.
_provenance.julian: Julian dates are computed from the Kali ahargaṇa by integer arithmetic (kala-dvara.js civilFromKaliDay) and re-checked by the test.
_provenance.sha256: Each record's 'sha256' is SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the record without that field (vedha-lekha.js sha256 and canonical); `node scripts/parampara-samskara.cjs --stamp` writes them, parampara.test.js checks them.
_provenance.tags: [text] stated by the source; [reading] this repository's reading of it; [standard] a convention of the tradition not stated in a local text; [paramparā] a historical record used as data; [owner-statement] the owner's attribution, no local edition; [unverified] not checkable here; [theorem] integer or exact arithmetic on the stated numbers; [claim-only] a claim in code or derived prose with no local source.

checks.what: Decoded units first (katapayadi.js), each vākya is rāśi|degrees|minutes|seconds|thirds; in thirds it equals (yuga revolutions mod 7500) × 10368 exactly for the Moon (3336), Mars (1824), Jupiter (4224), Saturn (4064) and the apogee (719), and for the node (7226) with the edition's printed 52″ (next check) — certifying the apogee and node integers 488,219 and 232,226 from a second text; Mercury's śīghra decodes to the whole residue 4520; 7500 × 210,389 = 1,577,917,500 (Āryabhaṭa's civil days)
Two vākyas decode one syllable off the edition's printed figures: Venus 3s25° against the printed 3s24° (= the whole residue 2388), and the node 72″ against the printed 52″ (the residue's)

Shifted labels: the e-text's English labels over the vākyas ('Sun:' over the first) run one body ahead; the verse itself says the list begins with the Moon (śītaraśmi-mukhyānām) and ends with the node; read in the verse's order the values reproduce the local integers

value.instruction: compute the eclipses Parameśvara cites, or others established by tradition and taught by one's own lineage; with these and those seen oneself, determine and announce the coming eclipse
